title: quantization-debug-scratchpad-int8-fp8-bf16-nan
content:
Goal: track investigation of sporadic NaNs and degraded quality after INT8 and experimental FP8 quantization on our Llama-like models. This is a working scratchpad — rough notes, commands tried, small logs, hypotheses, and next steps.

Summary of symptom:
- After enabling INT8 quantization (PACT + per-channel for weights) we saw ~0.7 perplexity regression on validation and occasional NaN token probabilities in long-context generation (~seq_len>1024).
- FP8 (E4M3) experiments show similar instability but less frequent NaNs; BF16 runs stable but costlier.
- NaNs appear in softmax outputs (logits) occasionally and sometimes earlier in KV-cache accumulation for long contexts.

Environment:
- Serving runtime branch: git rev HEAD = 3f2a1b9 (serving/quant-int8-experiments)
- CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS 12.1, drivers up-to-date
- Models: rwi-13b-2024 (transformer with RMSNorm, Rotary + ALiBi)
- Quant libs: custom kernel + tinc/quantize.py (per-channel scales saved as .scales)

Chronological notes:
2024-02-18 09:12 - initial repro-ran a batch of eval prompts (len 1536) with INT8 and saw NaN in logits for prompt id 42.
Command: python eval_perf.py --model rwi-13b-2024 --quant int8 --batch 2 --seq_len 1536 --seed 42
Snippet:
  WARNING: encountered NaN in logits at layer 21, head 7
  stack: runtime/attn_kernel.cu:line 402
  logits[1023] = NaN

I dumped intermediate tensors (layer 21 attention scores) to /tmp/dump/seed42/layer21/ and saw extremely large values ~1e38 before softmax; indicates overflow in attention score computation (q*k^T / sqrt(dk)).

2024-02-18 11:45 - quick mitigation test-scaled down Q,K by 1 / (1 + prefix_len/1024) before dot product in inference runtime (quick hack).
Result: NaN disappears for same input but output quality is worse (perplexity +1.2). Not acceptable.

Commands and logs tried:
- dump run (python eval_perf.py --dump-intermediates --limit 10)
- compare float32 vs int8 activations (script: tools/compare_activations.py --a float32 --b int8 --layer 21)
Observations:
  - Per-channel weight scaling seems OK (max scale ~0.02); but activation dynamic range in Q/K can be much smaller for some tokens and very large for others (outliers).
  - Quantized matmul output occasionally produced +-inf before downstream clamp. Kernel didn't clip infs.

2024-02-19 10:30 - hypothesis 1: accumulation precision and kernel ordering-INT8 matmul uses int32 accumulation in our kernel, then cast to float32. For very long seqs the reduction sum might overflow int32 if per-term values are large (unlikely but check).
Check command: inspect kernel accumulator type in runtime: cat runtime/kernels/quant_gemm.cu | grep Accum
Result: int32_t Accum; // confirmed
Note: int32 max ~2e9. If each multiply can be up to 1e6 and sum ~4096 terms, overflow possible -> yields incorrect huge values -> NaN downstream.

2024-02-19 13:20 - quick fix test: switch accumulator to int64 in local build
Commands:
  bazel build //runtime:quant_gemm --define ACCUM=64
  cp bazel-bin/runtime/quant_gemm.so runtime/plugins/
Test: python eval_perf.py --model rwi-13b-2024 --quant int8 --seq_len 1536 --batch 1
Result: No NaNs for the tested prompts. Perplexity improved back to near-fp32 baseline.
Caveat: int64 accumulation slower and uses more memory. Need microbenchmarks.

2024-02-20 09:00 - hypothesis 2: scale mismatch and per-channel vs per-tensor
- We store per-channel (out) scales for weight quantization but use per-tensor scale for activations (fast path). If activation outliers are present, matmul results can overshoot expected dynamic range.
- Test: run with per-channel activation scales (empirically compute per-head scale for Q/K outputs).
Commands:
  python tools/compute_activation_scales.py --model rwi-13b-2024 --layer 0-23 --type qk --out scales_act_head.npy
  python eval_perf.py --quant int8 --act-scales scales_act_head.npy --seq_len 1536
Result: reduced frequency of NaNs but still occasional. Points to multiple contributing factors (accum overflow + scaling).

2024-02-21 14:15 - FP8 experiments-built FP8 (E4M3) kernels (experimental) and ran same evals. Observed slightly fewer NaNs but more numerical instability in training-like ops (layernorm backward) — not an immediate concern for inference-only serving but indicates representation edge-cases.
Commands:
  python eval_perf.py --quant fp8-e4m3 --seq_len 1536 --dump-errors /tmp/fp8-dump
Logs:
  FP8: occasional subnormal floods (grad-like ops) and denorm handling slower, but softmax NaN frequency dropped by ~40% compared to INT8 baseline.

2024-02-22 10:05 - BF16 baseline-ran bf16 eval to sanity check; no NaNs, slightly higher memory but stable. Suggest BF16 as fallback tier for long-context heavy customers.

Error snippets and stack traces captured:
- runtime/attn_kernel.cu:402: value overflow in dot-product accumulate -> produced +-inf -> softmax sees NaN
- python runtime exception: ValueError: logits contain NaN (first occurrence at sample 7)
- GPU driver warning: cuBLAS status: CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED (when FP8 kernel used concurrently with other GPU ops)

Hypotheses summary:
- Primary cause: integer accumulator overflow in INT8 GEMM (int32 insufficient for long seq / large intermediate magnitudes) -> causes inf/NaN downstream.
- Secondary cause: activation scaling mismatch and heavy outliers for certain tokens/heads -> quantized outputs blow up if scales not per-head or input clamped.
- Tertiary cause: kernel code doesn't guard NaNs/inf (no clamps after accumulation), and softmax implementation does not robustly handle infs (should subtract max but inf breaks it).

Experiments that helped:
- Rebuilding kernel with int64 accumulator removed NaNs in repro cases.
- Switching to per-head activation scales reduced frequency but didn't fully remove.
- BF16 path entirely stable (good fallback).

Performance/microbenchmark notes:
- Int64 accumulation increases kernel time ~12-22% on A100 for matmul sizes relevant to attention (tested with bench/gemm_bench.py).
- Per-head activation scaling adds ~8% overhead (extra mem + load per head).

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Patch: conditionally use int64 accumulator for GEMM when (seq_len * max_abs_term) heuristics predict overflow. Implement runtime check with fast path. (owner: Evan)
- [ ] Implement post-accum clamp/NaN-to-max handling in kernel to prevent inf propagation (owner: Luca).
- [ ] Add per-head activation scaling option in config and evaluate cost/benefit across workloads (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Add automated fuzz tests that generate extreme token activations to catch overflow cases in CI (owner: SRE/serving).
- [ ] Document fallback policy: if NaN frequency > threshold -> switch session to BF16/fp32 automatically. (owner: product/ops)

Open questions:
- Is int64 accumulation acceptable for Dedicated customers with strict latency SLOs? Might need heuristic to selectively enable only for long-context sessions.
- Should we quantize using symmetric or asymmetric schemes for Q/K to reduce magnitude variance?
- Can we implement an online clamp that rescales Q/K based on running max per sequence to avoid global perf hit?

Notes for triage meeting:
- Bring microbench numbers comparing int32 vs int64 accumulation on our fleet (A100 vs H100).
- Show frequency distribution of activation magnitudes and heads (attach script output).
- Proposal: enable int64 accum for seq_len>1024 or when computed expected_accum > threshold (config flag at runtime).

Raw commands used during investigation (for reproducibility):
- bazel build //runtime:quant_gemm --define ACCUM=64
- python eval_perf.py --model rwi-13b-2024 --quant int8 --batch 1 --seq_len 1536 --dump-intermediates /tmp/dumps
- python tools/compare_activations.py --a float32 --b int8 --layer 21 --out /tmp/comp21.json
- python tools/compute_activation_scales.py --model rwi-13b-2024 --layer 0-23 --type qk --out /tmp/scales_head.npy
- python eval_perf.py --quant fp8-e4m3 --seq_len 1536 --dump-errors /tmp/fp8-dump

If reproducing: start with seed 42, seq_len 1536, batch 1. Watch for warnings in runtime logs: "encountered NaN in logits".

References:
- Notebook: confluence:Quantization-Playbook-v2 (section on accumulators)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842 (experimental FP8 kernels)

Scratch miscellaneous thoughts:
- Could use stochastic rounding for activations to reduce bias by extreme values; expensive but maybe just for edge-case sequences.
- Consider adaptive per-sequence rescaling: compute max(|Q|,|K|) per head for the prefix and apply a scalar shrink to keep dot-products in safe range. Might be cheap (one reduction per head).

End of scratchpad.
